reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about surface energies, diffusion kinetics, segregation, and evaporation in a novel five-component nanoparticle system, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific surface energies, diffusion behavior, or stability of this exact equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticle system under the stated conditions.
premises: Au and Cu have lower surface energies than Co, Ni, Pt in the alloy
Surface energy differences drive segregation of Au and Cu to nanoparticle surfaces above ~673 K
This segregation is kinetically controlled, not stabilized by entropy
Segregation causes reshaping and partial evaporation of Au/Cu
The baseline expectation for HEAs is sluggish diffusion and high thermal stability
